analysis.title: Economic and Market Overview, October 2026
key_insights: Treasury yields retraced much of September's rise in October: 10-year fell 36 bps to 4.93%, 2-year fell 30 bps to 4.59%, 30-year fell 32 bps to 5.31%.

The S&P 500 fell 0.9% in October to 7,580.07, with losses in the final two days after Alphabet's and Amazon's Q3 earnings alarmed investors already wary of capex plans. The equal-weighted index rose 5.0%, the Dow 1.8% and the Russell 2000 0.6%.
Credit spreads widened and the credit curve steepened. High yield OAS rose 29 bps to 340, long credit OAS rose 11 bps to 109, and intermediate credit OAS rose 9 bps to 74.
WTI rose 15.6% in October to $104.12, back above $100. Gold fell 6.8% to its lowest level of the year. The Dollar Index rose 0.4% to 101.88.
Investment-grade issuance was $125B in October (J.P. Morgan), 17% above the trailing four-October average. High-yield issuance was $14.6B, the lowest in 18 months.
Q3 GDP advance estimate was 3.4% annualized, 0.2 points above expectations and up from 2.2% in Q2. Personal consumption grew 3.8%, 0.4 points above forecasts.

September nonfarm payrolls rose 29k, 61k below expectations, and the prior two months were revised down by a combined 60k. Unemployment rose 0.1 point to 4.2% while participation rose 0.2 points to 61.8%.

September CPI was hot for the second month in a row. Headline rose 0.6% MoM (in line with expectations), core rose 0.3% MoM versus consensus of 0.2%. The strength came from energy, core goods and owners' equivalent rent, not wireless plans.
After the CPI release, the odds of an October rate hike were repriced to about 50% but fell to effectively zero by the 10/28 FOMC announcement. PCE measures matched estimates.

The FOMC held the policy rate at its October 27-28 meeting. Markets now price 80% odds of a December hike and one more hike in 2027. NISA expects one more hike in December and a March hike only if oil stays at or above current levels.
earnings_insights: Alphabet's and Amazon's Q3 earnings (reported by the end of October 2026) drew an alarmed investor reaction tied to capex plans, contributing to the S&P 500's decline in the last two days of the month. The report gives no EPS or revenue figures.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Market pricing now matches the most hawkish cohort of the FOMC dot plot. NISA expects one more hike in December and a March hike only if oil holds at or above current levels.

risk_factors: Oil at or above current levels (WTI $104.12) would keep the Fed on a hiking path into March.
Capex concerns around large-cap tech after Alphabet's and Amazon's earnings.
Hot inflation (core CPI above consensus) combined with weak payroll growth.
Wider credit spreads, especially at the long end, and heavy investment-grade supply.
vol_and_positioning: Risk-asset volatility persisted through October, and rate markets removed nearly two full hikes from the expected policy path through December 2027.
The breakeven curve flattened as shorter maturities followed oil higher while longer tenors fell.

tension_points.bull_case: Rate markets removed nearly two full hikes from the path through December 2027 as risk-asset volatility persisted, and the Fed held in October.
tension_points.bear_case: September CPI was hot for the second month, core rose above consensus, and markets price 80% odds of a December hike. WTI above $100 keeps inflation pressure on.
tension_points.what_invalidates: NISA expects a March hike only if oil prices remain at or above current levels, so a fall in oil would remove it.

theme_stances.key_argument: The Fed will hike once more in December and again in March only if oil prices remain at or above current levels.
theme_stances.evidence: the Fed will hike just once more in December
